chunks: Among such reports is the report of Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi (may Allah have mercy on him), from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:
Allah did not send any prophet except to prohibit wine, and to confess to Allah regarding al-Bada (that ﴿Indeed, Allah does whatever He pleases﴾), and that incense should be in his inheritance.

key_terms.الْبَدَاءُ: Al-Bada (the doctrine of divine manifestation/change of decree)
key_terms.﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ﴾: Quranic verse meaning 'Indeed, Allah does whatever He pleases'

ai.seo_question: What are the three key elements of the prophets' mission mentioned by Imam al-Rida regarding wine, divine decree, and inheritance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (a.s.) identifies the prohibition of wine and the affirmation of al-Bada (divine alteration of decree) as universal missions of all prophets, linking the latter to the Quranic verse 'Indeed, Allah does whatever He pleases' (13:39). This narration, found in Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, underscores the continuity of prophetic teachings regarding divine sovereignty and includes the specific detail that incense (kandar) was part of the prophets' inheritance, reflecting their distinct spiritual and material legacy.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 419 - Among such reports is the report of Muhammad bin Ja’far Asadi narrating from Ali bin Ibrahim from Rayan bin Sult that he said: I heard Imam Ridha (a.s) say:
Allah, the Mighty and the High did not send any prophet, but to prohibit wine, to confess in Bada from Almighty Allah and that He can do whatever He likes; and that He has advised the use of incense.
